title: Quality & Moat Screen — Nasdaq-100 ∪ S&P 500 constituents
file_stem: Quality & Moat Screen – Nasdaq-100 ∪ S&P 500 (as of 2026-10-31)
roic_note: 10Y Avg ROIC carried over from v1 ('Ref: 10Y Avg ROIC'); v1 did not document its source.
universe_text: Universe as of 2026-10-31: S&P 500 (Wikipedia "List of S&P 500 companies", revision 2026-10-27 03:50 CET; 503 securities) ∪ Nasdaq-100 (Wikipedia "List of NASDAQ-100 companies", revision 2026-10-24 11:15 CEST; 101 securities) = 518 tickers → 515 companies after merging share classes (GOOGL/GOOG, FOXA/FOX, NWSA/NWS). GICS sector/sub-industry from the S&P 500 list; the 15 Nasdaq-100-only names have a GICS-equivalent mapped by hand, marked "(mapped)".
caveat: CAVEAT: This is a qualitative screen, not investment advice and not a valuation. Scores are judgements based on each company's business model and public knowledge as of October 2026; they can be wrong or out of date, and a PASS says nothing about whether the share price is attractive. Verify before acting.
how_produced: 1. All 515 companies were grouped into ~125 GICS sub-industries. For each sub-industry a baseline score was set for every criterion (industry-level traits: need permanence, essentiality, repeatability, trajectory, technology/substitution risk, structure).

2. Each company was then adjusted from that baseline for its own position: market share and rank, customer concentration, supplier/labour dependence, switching costs, barrier type, management record and pricing history.

3. Scoring was done in industry batches for consistency, then cross-checked across industries. Confidence (H/M/L) flags names where the judgement is less certain (recent spin-offs, IPOs, turnarounds, crypto/AI-cycle names).

4. The 'Ref:' metric columns on Inputs do not feed any score; since v2 they drive the P5 data check on Screen, which flags disagreement for review: pulled from SEC EDGAR XBRL "frames" (calendar-year aligned, FY2015–FY2025 where available). Revenue CAGR = first to last available year; NI down-years = years net income fell vs prior year; Gross-margin range = max − min gross margin in percentage points; Inventory − revenue growth = inventory CAGR minus revenue CAGR (pp; positive = inventory growing faster than sales). "n/a" = no comparable US-GAAP USD data (foreign filers ASML, TRI, FER, CCEP, PDD, NBIS; banks/insurers without gross margin or inventory; recent listings).
5. Rationale = short analyst note. Since v2 the list of criteria scored 0 is computed live on Screen ('Weak points') instead of being typed into the note.
sources: Sources: Wikipedia constituent lists (above); SEC EDGAR XBRL API (data.sec.gov); company filings and public reporting for business-model facts; S&P Dow Jones Indices press releases for 2026 index changes (e.g. Vylor spin from Corteva, Vivmark = Equity Residential + AvalonBay, Everpure = Pure Storage, Skydance = Paramount Skydance).
